text.p: Italian debt market held to lower levels in late trading due to concerns over the debate surrounding Italy's adherence to the Maastricht Treaty and a European single currency, dealers said.

Futures were troubled by a debate over Italy's committment to European political and monetary union which was involving members of the Italian cabinet, but Prime Minister Romano Prodi stressed today that Italy will hold firm on its determination to pursue the goal of a European currency union.
"The market is clearly worried as the debate is drawing in senior members of the Italian cabinet," said one Milan-based futures trader.
Investor sentiment was also hurt by the lower dollar and the slide in U.S. T-bonds, but trading in BTP futures was generally thin with London's LIFFE market closed for a bank holiday.

The market was initially rattled after Prodi's deputy Walter Veltroni said Italy and other EU countries should re-consider the criteria and timing of monetary union, amid some worries that the strick EMU criteria could push Italy into recession.

Dealers said that this fresh debate only added to worries that are already pre-occupying investors with the Italian government facing battles this autumn over its 1997 financial budget, jobs and privatisations.
